key_insight: Use the model's own uncertainty at test time to decide whether and how much to zoom into a GUI region, so only genuinely ambiguous queries get high-resolution reprocessing rather than applying fixed crops to everything.
problem_solved: Improves localization of small icons and elements in dense GUI layouts while avoiding wasted computation from uniform, fixed-size zoom-in schemes that ignore per-instance uncertainty.
method: Estimate per-query/per-instance uncertainty from the base GUI-grounding model at test time (no additional training).
If uncertainty exceeds a threshold, generate one or more adaptive crops with variable scale/position focused on uncertain regions and re-run the grounding model at higher resolution.
Fuse the high-resolution predictions back into the original image coordinates and accept the refined output only when uncertainty is reduced.
impact: Provides a plug-and-play, training-free way to boost accuracy on hard GUI grounding cases (small icons, cluttered layouts) while saving computation compared to blanket zoom-in strategies — easy to adopt in existing pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: base inference → uncertainty scoring → conditional adaptive cropping → high-res re-inference → final fusion
Side-by-side UI screenshot: original prediction vs adaptive zoom prediction highlighting corrected small-icon localization
Bar/line chart: accuracy vs compute showing adaptive zoom-in outperforming uniform zoom-in for same or less cost
Confidence/uncertainty heatmaps overlaid on screenshots to visualize where the model requests zoom
paper_title: UI-Zoomer: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Zoom-In for GUI Grounding
paper_authors: Fei Tang, Bofan Chen, Zhengxi Lu, Tongbo Chen, Songqin Nong
